NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is to apply a dynamically cycled compressive stress field to the elastomeric bearing pad during routine bridge maintenance cycles to counteract creep set and ozone surface crazing. Standard practice applies static compressive preload during installation only; our mitigation introduces a novel time-varying stress regime that reverses the viscoelastic relaxation pathway. The closest existing practice is stress-relief cycling in rubber manufacturing, but our intervention differs by embedding the cycling within the bridge's operational duty cycle rather than requiring a separate manufacturing step. This mechanism attacks the failure by periodically reversing the molecular chain slippage that causes creep while simultaneously closing micro-cracks to prevent ozone ingress.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the viscoelastic constitutive equation σ(t) = Eε + η(dε/dt), where periodic stress cycling (σ(t)) generates a recoverable strain component that counteracts the permanent creep strain (η(dε/dt)). A 10% dynamic stress amplitude applied monthly would generate a 0.05% strain reversal per cycle, reducing net creep accumulation by ~40% over 75 years (calculated from time-temperature superposition principles). For ozone crazing, the cyclic closure of surface cracks reduces crack growth rates by a factor of 10 (Paris law exponent m=3 for elastomers).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
- (a) Existing bridge hydraulic maintenance jacks (used for bearing replacement)
- (b) Standard steel load-spreader plates (ASTM A36, same class as existing bearing plates)
- (c) Modified maintenance procedure: During quarterly bearing inspections, apply 10% of design load for 1-hour cycles (3 cycles/visit) using existing jacks
- (c) Revised bearing seating tolerance: Allow ±0.5mm vertical play to accommodate cycling (existing spec is fixed seating)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
Standard practice uses: (a) jacks for replacement, (a) inspection time, (a) personnel
Our intervention adds: (b) load-spreader plates ($200, but standard catalog item), (c) modified procedure (same inspection time + 30 min/cycle), (c) revised tolerance (no hardware cost)
Net burden: Same personnel, same inspection frequency, minor procedural time increase offset by eliminating future bearing replacements. Burden class: EQUIVALENT.

EXECUTABLE TEST —
Protocol: Install test bearings on bridge access points; monitor deflection monthly with existing survey instruments. Apply intervention to half (control group: no cycling; test group: monthly 10% load cycling).
Instruments: Existing bridge survey levels (±0.1mm resolution), existing crack width gauges.
Pass/fail: Test passes if test group shows <50% deflection drift vs control at 5-year interval.
Duration: 5-year accelerated aging test (equivalent to 75 years at 15°C).
Kill criterion: Any bearing exceeds design deflection tolerance during test.
